subject: mathematics
correct_idea: (a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2: multiply the bracket by itself

subject: mathematics
misconception: does not do the same operation to both sides of an equation
correct_idea: an equation stays true only if both sides get the same operation

subject: mathematics
misconception: cancels terms in a sum, e.g. (x+3)/3 = x
correct_idea: only common FACTORS cancel, not terms that are added

subject: mathematics
misconception: sign errors when subtracting a negative number
correct_idea: subtracting a negative is the same as adding the positive

subject: mathematics
misconception: adds fractions by adding numerators and denominators (1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5)
correct_idea: fractions need a common denominator before the numerators are added

subject: mathematics
misconception: thinks a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
correct_idea: the bigger the denominator, the smaller each piece

subject: mathematics
misconception: mixes up area and perimeter
correct_idea: perimeter is the distance around; area is the space inside (square units)

subject: mathematics
misconception: multiplies the exponents when multiplying powers with the same base
correct_idea: x^a * x^b = x^(a+b): add the exponents

subject: mathematics
misconception: sqrt(a + b) = sqrt(a) + sqrt(b)
correct_idea: square roots do not split over addition

subject: mathematics
misconception: mixes up opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse because the triangle is turned
correct_idea: opposite and adjacent are named from the angle you are looking at

subject: mathematics
misconception: reads the gradient as run over rise
correct_idea: gradient = rise over run = change in y over change in x

subject: mathematics
misconception: differentiates a constant and gets the constant back
correct_idea: the derivative of a constant is 0

subject: mathematics
misconception: adds probabilities of independent events when both must happen
correct_idea: for 'A and B' (independent) multiply; for 'A or B' (mutually exclusive) add

subject: natural_sciences
misconception: heavier objects fall faster in a vacuum
correct_idea: without air resistance all objects fall with the same acceleration

subject: natural_sciences
misconception: mass and weight are the same thing
correct_idea: mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the force of gravity on it (N)

subject: natural_sciences
misconception: the seasons happen because the Earth is closer to the Sun in summer
correct_idea: seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis

subject: physical_sciences
misconception: current is used up as it goes through a resistor
correct_idea: current is the same all the way round a series circuit; energy is transferred

subject: physical_sciences
misconception: a moving object needs a constant force to keep moving
correct_idea: with no net force an object keeps its velocity (Newton's first law)

subject: physical_sciences
misconception: forgets to convert units (g to kg, km/h to m/s) before substituting
correct_idea: convert to SI units first, then substitute

subject: life_sciences
misconception: plants get their food from the soil
correct_idea: plants make food by photosynthesis; the soil gives water and minerals

subject: life_sciences
misconception: confuses mitosis and meiosis
correct_idea: mitosis makes identical body cells; meiosis makes gametes with half the chromosomes

subject: english
misconception: mixes up their, there and they're
correct_idea: their = belongs to them; there = a place; they're = they are

subject: english
misconception: uses an apostrophe to make a plural (apple's)
correct_idea: apostrophes show belonging or a missing letter, not plurals

subject: english
misconception: copies whole sentences from the text instead of answering in own words
correct_idea: find the evidence, then say it in your own words for each mark

subject: english
misconception: confuses simile and metaphor
correct_idea: a simile compares using 'like' or 'as'; a metaphor says one thing IS another

subject: afrikaans
misconception: keeps the verb in second position after 'dat' (as in a main clause)
correct_idea: in a subordinate clause the verb goes to the end

subject: afrikaans
misconception: uses only one 'nie' in a negative sentence
correct_idea: Afrikaans uses a double negative: ...nie ... nie

subject: afrikaans
misconception: forms the past tense with an English-style ending
correct_idea: the perfect tense uses het + ge- + verb (ek het geloop)
